ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels with approximately 10-15% high-intensity (white/light-yellow) pixels appearing as localized speckles and mottling.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Numerous small, high-contrast circular blobs (mottling) scattered across both lobes. Concentrations of higher-intensity grey-white pixels are localized at the distal tips. Several linear white streaks are mapped near the central axial region at the base of the fluke.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an interior angle of approximately 65 degrees; the notch depth is roughly 15% of the total vertical height of the visible fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations (peaks and valleys) with amplitudes varying between 2 and 15 pixels along the continuous trailing edge. The innermost margins of the lobes show deeper, more jagged depressions.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Outer edges exhibit a consistent convex curve originating from the median notch and extending toward the distal tips, which terminate in irregular, pointed geometries.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Numerous localized circular clusters (5-15 pixel diameters) of high-contrast yellow-white pixels are distributed across both lobes, with a high-density concentration at the right distal tip.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A distinct diagonal linear pixel disruption is visible on the inner right lobe. Smaller, vertically-oriented linear marks are detected near the central peduncle attachment point.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive irregular pixel clusters and ragged tissue at both distal tips, consistent with heavy barnacle colonization or historic physical trauma.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly irregular and tattered appearance of the distal-most lobe margins compared to the smoother leading edge curvature.
